# giong

> A thread-per-core async runtime for Rust on Linux, built directly on io_uring. Every
> worker owns its ring, tasks and buffers; tasks never move between threads, so futures
> need not be `Send`. Version 0.4.0.

Facts that are easy to get wrong:

- Linux only: io_uring on 6.0 or newer, and an epoll driver where io_uring is blocked
  (Docker's default seccomp profile, gVisor) or the kernel is older. It does not build on
  macOS or Windows yet.
- Buffers are passed by value and handed back, because the kernel uses them after the call:
  `stream.write_all(buf).await` returns `(io::Result<()>, buf)`.
- `recv` is cancel safe: a `timeout` around it loses no data. A dropped `write_all` may
  have sent part of its buffer.
- There are no macros: start a runtime with `giong::block_on` or `giong::Builder`.
- An error giong raises starts with a code, such as `GIONG-E0102`, says how to fix it, and
  links to its page; `giong::error::code(&err)` returns the code to match on.
- giong-web: build the `Router` inside each worker's future (`run(|_| async { .. })`), since
  an `App` is not `Send`. A handler is `async fn(Req<S>) -> Result<Response, Error>`; `?` on
  any other error answers `500` and logs the cause, never sending it.
- Install with `cargo add giong` (and `giong-http`, `giong-web`, ...). Libraries need Rust 1.80.

## Docs

- [giong API](https://docs.rs/giong): Gióng — a thread-per-core async runtime for Linux, built on io_uring, with an epoll fallback
- [giong-tls API](https://docs.rs/giong-tls): TLS for the giong thread-per-core runtime, built on rustls
- [giong-http API](https://docs.rs/giong-http): A small, strict HTTP/1.1 server and client for the giong thread-per-core runtime
- [giong-postgres API](https://docs.rs/giong-postgres): A PostgreSQL client and connection pool for the giong thread-per-core runtime
- [giong-mysql API](https://docs.rs/giong-mysql): A MySQL client and connection pool for the giong thread-per-core runtime
- [giong-redis API](https://docs.rs/giong-redis): A Redis client, pipelining across tasks, with Pub/Sub and a pool, for the giong thread-per-core runtime
- [giong-web API](https://docs.rs/giong-web): A router, middleware and JSON for HTTP services on the giong thread-per-core runtime
- [giong-mcp API](https://docs.rs/giong-mcp): An MCP server that lets AI agents look inside a running giong service: workers, tasks, pools, profiles
- [giong-compat API](https://docs.rs/giong-compat): Tokio and futures-io I/O traits for giong's streams, so transport-generic protocol crates run on giong
- [Get started](https://giong.run/docs/): requirements, a first server, examples, limits
- [README](https://github.com/giong-run/Giong/blob/main/README.md): design, benchmarks with their method, limitations
- [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/giong-run/Giong/blob/main/AGENTS.md): how to build, test and change giong, for coding agents
- [Error codes](https://github.com/giong-run/Giong/blob/main/docs/errors/README.md): what each `GIONG-E` code means and how to fix it
- [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/giong-run/Giong/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md): the rules every change follows
- [ROADMAP.md](https://github.com/giong-run/Giong/blob/main/ROADMAP.md): milestones and deliberate non-goals
- [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/giong-run/Giong/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md): what changed in each release

## Examples

- [examples/echo.rs](https://github.com/giong-run/Giong/blob/main/examples/echo.rs): A TCP echo server on every core.
- [examples/http.rs](https://github.com/giong-run/Giong/blob/main/examples/http.rs): A small HTTP/1.1 server: keep-alive, pipelining, idle timeouts, a header size limit and graceful shutdown on SIGINT and SIGTERM. The same routes the benchmarks use.
- [examples/udp_echo.rs](https://github.com/giong-run/Giong/blob/main/examples/udp_echo.rs): A UDP echo server, receiving with multishot recvmsg.
- [examples/cat.rs](https://github.com/giong-run/Giong/blob/main/examples/cat.rs): Prints files to standard output, reading them through io_uring with positional reads.

- [Benchmark results](https://github.com/giong-run/Giong/tree/main/bench/results): raw numbers behind the README
